title: Causal Ripple Lane — execution inspection lens for related inference requests
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design and prototype a new request-inspection UI pattern called 'Causal Ripple Lane' for Redwood Console. Goal: enable engineers and SREs to quickly understand causal relationships between inference requests across services, routes, and model variants using a compact, time-aware lane view. The lane visualizes each related request as a ripple (adaptive width = token count, color = outcome) laid out along a shared time axis. Secondary detail panes show span groups, KV cache hits, model variant, route metadata, and per-request cost estimates. The view should support filtering, pinning a root request, and toggling between a compact ripple lane and an expanded contextual timeline with span detail. This ticket captures the first-round prototype, design rationale, trade-offs, acceptance criteria, and planned usability testing.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates placing a selected root request at center with at least 20 related requests displayed as ripples along +/- 10s range
UX supports filtering by model, route, status (ok/error), latency percentile, and cost above a threshold
Clicking a ripple opens a right-side span-detail pane with span list, correlation id, KV cache metrics, and link to raw trace payload
Keyboard navigation between ripples (left/right) and accessible labels for screen readers implemented in prototype annotations
Design spec includes failure-mode behaviors (e.g., high-volume collapse, summarization, and pagination) and fallback to compact list view
designer_notes: Motivation: current waterfall/timeline metaphors are verbose for dense traffic burst analysis. The ripple metaphor emphasizes lineage and resource impact while keeping a single axis for time. We intentionally compress span internals into hover/side panes to reduce visual noise. Performance constraint: prototype should be feasible to implement using existing console charts stack (React + D3-lite) without introducing heavy animation that blocks main thread.
tradeoffs: Pros: better at surfacing clusters of causally related requests and quick triage of burst patterns
Cons: may obscure micro-span ordering and per-service call stacks unless explicitly expanded
Implementation risk: requires efficient client-side summarization to avoid rendering thousands of ripples; propose server-side pre-aggregation for >500 related requests
Accessibility: using color+shape; must ensure patterns also encode status via texture/outline and aria labels for non-visual users
open_questions: Should ripple width map to token count or estimated compute cost? (asked the infra team for cost mapping guidance)
How to define 'related' requests heuristically? correlation-id only, or additional causal signals (parent span, request headers)?
Acceptable collapse threshold for high traffic: 200 related items? 500? Need product decision tied to Dedicated customer SLAs
Should we include an explicit model-variant breadcrumb to support canary rollouts investigation?
comments: 2026-02-26 - Avery Chen: Initial sketch uploaded to Figma. Focused on compact layout and hover-to-expand interactions.
2026-03-01 - Samir Patel (Eng): Reviewed prototype. Suggest server-side pre-aggregation and sampling strategy for >250 related requests. Concern about animation cost on low-end browsers.
2026-03-03 - Luis Martinez (PM): Aligning with rollout debug workflows. Requested an explicit 'pin to rollout' action to surface model-variant and commit hashes for canary investigation.
2026-03-05 - Accessibility review (Nina Jacobs): Recommend non-color encodings for status and explicit aria-label templates. Added keyboard navigation notes to spec.
2026-03-09 - Design critique: general positive feedback; reviewers asked for an alternate collapsed list view for archived traces and a contextual cost-sparkline beside each ripple.
2026-03-10 - Nina Jacobs: Updated prototype to include cost-estimate micro sparklines and added 'collapse by service' control. Preparing files for usability testing scheduled 2026-03-16.
usability_testing_plan: Recruit 6 participants from internal SRE/Platform teams. Tasks: 1) Identify root cause of 95th-percentile latency regression using ripple lane; 2) Find the model variant causing increased cost; 3) Use keyboard to navigate related requests. Metrics: task completion, time-to-answer, errors, and qualitative confidence. Test date: 2026-03-16.
implementation_notes: Front-end: componentized RippleLane + RippleItem + SpanDetailPane. Add server-side endpoint /traces/related?root_id=...&window=10s that returns compact summary entries (id, start_ts, duration_ms, token_count, status, model_variant, cost_est). Backward compatibility: if server endpoint unavailable, fall back to client-side correlation-id grouping of raw traces.
review_outcome: In Review — awaiting engineering feasibility confirmation on pre-aggregation endpoint and product decision on collapse thresholds. Aiming for alpha behind feature flag in console-2026.03 release.
